description: Add a part and make it the active part before returning. The part starts empty (no seed cube): the first insert_* creates the body. The result partId is a new opaque surf id, not the previously active part. When script is set, that script runs before the call returns (ok, errors, failures, status); a failed script still leaves the part. Agent calls default to the assembly origin; pass position [x,y,z] mm only as a rough block-out. A position, in an assembly of two or more parts, adds warning { code: "unjointed_part", part_id, hint } when the new part is in no joint; the call still succeeds. Working copy only: nothing reaches git without git_save. Build in ribbon order: block out every part of the assembly as plain blocks first (within seconds of the prompt, then screenshot for the user), then Build and Shape, then Polish, then pattern and place; finish each stage across the whole assembly before the next. Features first: insert_code_snippet { gap, why, script } is the fallback for one operation no feature can do (its block starts with // FEATURE-GAP: <missing feature or option> | <why the existing feature did not work>); set_script only rewrites a whole part. Hardware is one part per unique fastener type, one instance patterned to every place it goes. Fix one base part with a fixed joint, then place every part that touches or attaches to another with joint_create (one call creates the joint and solves placement). Use part_set_transform only for parts that touch nothing. Block-out positions are rough; joints set final positions. Takes return: "status" | "summary" | "full" (MCP default "status": status.script is omitted; "summary" adds status.features; "full" echoes the script).

position.description: Optional rough block-out translation [x, y, z] mm. Agent create_part defaults to the assembly origin; UI creation still staggers along +X. joint_create sets the final placement of a part that touches another. In an assembly of two or more parts, a position on a part that is in no joint returns warning unjointed_part and the call still succeeds.

return.description: How much of status to return: "status" drops status.script, "summary" drops it and adds status.features (the feature strip), "full" keeps the whole script. Over MCP the default is "status"; in the page it is "full". Read the script with get_script.

name: create_part
